record.paper_title: Several Open Problems in Operator Theory
record.original_question: Fix a positive integer m. A bounded linear operator T on a Hilbert space is an m-isometry when it satisfies sum_{k=0}^m (-1)^(m-k) binomial(m,k) (T*)^k T^k = 0, where T* is the adjoint of T. Is there a universal m-isometry A in L(K), on some Hilbert space K, such that every m-isometry T on a separable Hilbert space H is unitarily equivalent to the restriction A|M for some A-invariant subspace M of K?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a positive integer m. A bounded linear operator T on a complex Hilbert space H is called an m-isometry if
  sum_{k=0}^{m} (-1)^{m-k} C(m,k) (T*)^k T^k = 0,
where T* denotes the Hilbert-space adjoint of T and C(m,k) is the binomial coefficient. Given two bounded operators A on a Hilbert space K and B on a Hilbert space H, B is said to be unitarily equivalent to the restriction A|_M (for some closed A-invariant subspace M ⊆ K) if there exists a unitary operator U : H → M such that A U = U B.

Question: Does there exist a Hilbert space K and a bounded linear operator A on K such that A is an m-isometry and, for every separable complex Hilbert space H and every m-isometry T on H, there is a closed A-invariant subspace M ⊆ K with T unitarily equivalent to A|_M? (Such an A would be called a universal m-isometry.)
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not locate a published resolution to the question of existence of a universal m-isometry in the sense that every m-isometry on a separable Hilbert space is unitarily equivalent to its restriction to an invariant subspace. While there is active research on m-isometries and on Rota-type universal operators (with the latter producing similarity, not unitary equivalence), no source confirming or refuting this specific question was found.

status_evidence.title: Rota's universal operators and invariant subspaces in Hilbert spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Rota proved in 1960 that on a separable infinite dimensional Hilbert space there are universal operators; every operator is similar to a multiple of the restriction of a universal operator to one of its invariant subspaces.
status_evidence.claim: Existing universality results yield similarity to a scalar multiple, not unitary equivalence to a restriction, so they do not directly answer the m-isometry version.

status_evidence.title: Analytic m-isometries without the wandering subspace property
status_evidence.snippet: Active research on structural properties of m-isometric operators on Hilbert spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Research on m-isometries is ongoing, but no source resolving the universal m-isometry question was located.
